priorities.name: Quiet, private space for focus and confidential work
priorities.issue: Associates cannot reliably find quiet or private space for concentrated work and confidential conversations; even managers with designated space report having to leave their seat for a booth. This is the site's single largest driver of dissatisfaction.
whatItLooksLike: even with designated manager/director space, there is still minimal privacy and sensitive conversations require you to get up and move to a privacy booth which is inconvenient and disruptive.
Working at a pulse point is challenging due to potential missing items and high noise levels.

evidence.text: Focused / Private Work is the #1 priority category (priority score 79/100).
Friction for focused individual work is 37/100 — 64% feel under-supported; discretion 27/100 (50%).
Noise & Distraction: 137 comments, 68% negative. Privacy & Confidentiality: 100 comments, 55% negative.
Reserved seats lose value when the surrounding environment doesn't support the work done there.

priorities.proposedAction: Assess current quiet/phone-booth/enclosed-room capacity against peak demand; determine whether booking limits, an etiquette/quiet-zone protocol, or added enclosed capacity is the right fix before proposing construction.
priorities.siteMustDo: Walk the floor at peak occupancy, log where and when private/quiet space runs out, compare with booth/room utilization, and escalate a capacity gap to Workplace Solutions with evidence.

priorities.name: Desk reservation reliability and arrival readiness
priorities.issue: Desk reservations and the state of reserved workstations don't consistently hold up, so associates lose time getting set up when they arrive.
whatItLooksLike: Often cords or mouses are missing from desks and I do not know who to contact

evidence.text: Desk Availability & Reservations is the highest-volume theme: 174 comments, 53% negative.
Physical Environment ranks #2 by priority score (71/100).

priorities.proposedAction: Review booking rules and no-show behavior, and stand up a clear, visible path for reporting a desk found missing equipment on arrival.
priorities.siteMustDo: Audit a sample of reservations against actual occupancy for two weeks, confirm the failure mode (double-booking vs. no-shows vs. setup), and post the who-to-contact path at each neighborhood.

priorities.name: Workstation equipment reliability
priorities.issue: Monitors, cords and peripherals at shared desks are frequently missing or misconfigured, interrupting work.
whatItLooksLike: The limited availability of capsule rooms with dual monitors. There are times I have presentations to facilitate, and I cannot find an empty capsule room (others working in them for longer than an hour.) and pods do not have monitors in…

evidence.text: A recurring per-desk reliability issue rather than a one-off failure.

priorities.proposedAction: Institute a routine equipment check for shared workstations and standardize the docking/monitor setup so any desk works the same way on arrival.
priorities.siteMustDo: Inspect a sample of workstations, catalog missing/broken peripherals and reset-monitor issues, and set a recurring check with Technology.

protectWhatIsWorking.evidence: 91% positive across 22 comments — security/front-desk is a genuine strength
protectWhatIsWorking.note: Maintain the current service level and monitor performance.

assumptions: Quiet/enclosed-space utilization data isn't in the survey; an onsite walkthrough is needed to size any capacity gap before recommending build-out.
Woodland Hills is the lowest-ranked site overall (10 of 10); these three priorities target its largest, most-cited gaps first.
